sections.html:
Home values here center on $479,600, and 55.8 percent of households own their place. Roughly 229,816 people live in Tacoma, the Pierce County seat and a hub for the whole South Sound. If a tenant lives in your house, the median rent to compare against is $1,676.

Joint Base Lewis-McChord sits a few miles south, and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport is 22 miles north in SeaTac. Residents average 28.8 minutes getting to work, which is a fair selling point in a listing description.

Expect the first question from a buyer to be which part of Tacoma the house is in. Locals sort the city into Central Tacoma, New Tacoma around downtown, North Tacoma, Northeast Tacoma, West Tacoma and the Port of Tacoma area.

  • Central Tacoma: Hilltop, Delong Park, the Wedge, Bryant and College Heights.
  • North Tacoma: the Proctor District, the North Slope, Old Tacoma, Ruston Way, Skyline and Yakima Hill.
  • West Tacoma: the Highlands, Narrows, Titlow and Salmon Beach.
  • Downtown: the Stadium District, the Theater District, the Dome District and the Thea Foss Waterway.

Transit adds value near the core. The T Line links Tacoma Dome Station, downtown, the University of Washington Tacoma campus and Hilltop, while Sounder trains and express buses head toward Seattle.

Two boundary quirks matter. Ruston is its own incorporated town and Browns Point is unincorporated, so find out who has authority over your parcel before phoning Tacoma's permit desk. Older homes may also fall inside one of the five historic overlay zones. The city's preservation program covers 165 landmarks and more than 1,000 historic properties, so ask before planning any exterior change.

Water and slope define much of Tacoma. Ground rises from sea level to roughly 500 feet around Commencement Bay, and plenty of streets have Mount Rainier views. Low ground by the Port of Tacoma lies in the path of a Puyallup River lahar should the volcano erupt, a topic some tide-flat buyers raise.

The smell once nicknamed the Tacoma Aroma disappeared after the Simpson Tacoma Kraft mill shut in September 2023. Downtown has been rebuilt since the 1990s around the UW Tacoma campus, the T Line and a restored Thea Foss Waterway. The Tacoma Narrows bridges tie the city to Gig Harbor and the Kitsap Peninsula.

Tacoma's new property maintenance standard begins January 1, 2027. Under Ordinance 29125, International Property Maintenance Code standards join the city's Property Maintenance and Nuisance Code, and the city gets stronger tools against repeat and chronic violations.

Staff handle about 4,500 maintenance cases a year under Chapters 8.30 and 2.01. Section 7 holds the expanded enforcement program until at least nine months after the council funds it, so how much changes day to day depends on later budgets.

Owners of vacant, neglected or tenant-occupied houses should ask whether a complaint is open against the property before listing. Details are at tacoma.gov/IPMC.

Tax bills for Tacoma addresses come from the Assessor-Treasurer, 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, phone (253) 798-6111. Closing settles whatever is unpaid and divides the year between you and the buyer, so ask for a payoff number well ahead.

  • Pay online through the parcel search site.
  • Pay by phone at (253) 798-3333.
  • Mail a check to Pierce County Finance.
  • Walk in at the cashier lobby, 1501 Market St., Suite 120, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

A state program expands in January 2027 and will lower taxes for more Pierce County owners who are 61 or older or who have a qualifying disability. If you or a relative who owns the house might qualify, ask the Assessor-Treasurer before you sell.

sections.h2: Excise tax and the seller disclosure
sections.html:
Excise tax on the sale is the seller's bill, payable to the county treasurer when the sale occurs. The state takes 1.1 percent of the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent of what falls between $525,000 and $1,525,000, then a local share goes on top.

State law adds a paperwork duty. Under RCW 64.06.020 you hand the buyer a signed property condition form within five business days after the contract is signed. Questions run through the roof, plumbing, electrical and heating, and the form reminds you that carbon monoxide alarms and a smoke detection device are required.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
• Locate the newest tax statement and any special assessment notices.
  • Ask the county what it would take to clear unpaid tax.
  • Dig out permits for jobs such as a garage conversion or added bathroom.
  • Confirm nothing is open against the parcel at the city or county.

Put these in a single folder before showings begin. Buyers and title staff will request most of them, and whatever title work uncovers is paid from your proceeds, so learning the amounts now helps you plan.

Once you accept an offer, a few things happen in a fixed order. The disclosure statement goes to the buyer within five business days of the signed contract. Title or escrow orders payoffs for any unpaid property tax and any lien, and the property tax for the current year is prorated so each side covers its own months of ownership.

On the day of sale, the excise tax goes to the county treasurer. Because the state portion is graduated and the local share varies, ask your closing agent for the exact total before you sign instead of guessing from the rates above.

In a cash sale there is no lender, so no appraisal and no loan committee. That removes the most common reason a deal slips. What remains is title work, any open permit or code complaint, and your own moving date, which is why those items are worth sorting out first.

sections.h2: Should I list my Tacoma house or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
Think about your repair budget, your calendar and what a buyer's inspector would find. Listing puts the house in front of the whole market. A cash offer gives up some of that reach for speed and fewer strings, which suits a vacant home, an inherited one or a rental with tenants still inside.

Compare written offers by your net, not the top-line figure. Ask who pays excise tax, how long the offer is good for, when closing would happen and whether the buyer accepts the house and its contents as they sit. With no lender involved, there is no appraisal or loan approval to wait on, so timing comes down to title work and your move.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Tacoma that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer may take the house in its current condition. On most residential sales you still fill out the seller disclosure describing what you know about the property.

faqs.q: What does Ordinance 29125 mean for Tacoma sellers?
faqs.a: It sets a new maintenance standard starting January 1, 2027. Expanded enforcement begins no sooner than nine months after the council funds it, so look for open code complaints before you sell.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a Tacoma house?
faqs.a: Pierce County, through the Assessor-Treasurer's office in Tacoma. Call (253) 798-6111 about values, statements and exemptions, and ask for a payoff before closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax when a Tacoma house sells?
faqs.a: Usually the seller, to the county treasurer on the sale date. The state rate steps up, beginning at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, and a local share is added.

faqs.q: How many people live in Tacoma?
faqs.a: About 229,816 as of July 1, 2025, up from 219,346 at the April 2020 count. It is the third most populous city in Washington.
